description: Left internal by fz-go4.48 (deliberately, as an ambiguous site). apply_bit_spec_modifier's final fallback 'unsupported quoted bit-spec fragment kind {:?}' (quoted_function.rs ~:1344) fires when a bitstring type-spec segment's AST tag is neither call/INT/ATOM/BITSTRING/PROCBIN -- e.g. a FLOAT or LIST/tuple literal in modifier position like '<<x :: 3.14>>'. Bitstring segments are parsed as fully generic exprs upstream (frontdoor parse_bitstring_literal), so this arm is PROBABLY user-reachable via a plain typo, in which case it should be QuotedSourceError::user (parse/bitstring-bad-modifier) not ::new (internal). UNCONFIRMED: need to check whether float/list/tuple/map literals in modifier position actually reach THIS arm via a valid parse, versus being caught earlier by ast_node()/is_list_like. TASK: trace it; if user-reachable, reclassify to parse/bitstring-bad-modifier with a fixture proving '<<x :: 3.14>>'-style typos surface as user diagnostics; if genuinely internal (can't arise from valid parse), leave ::new and document why. Small, follow-up to fz-go4.48.
title: Confirm whether the bitstring 'unsupported fragment kind' fallback is user-reachable (float/list/tuple in modifier position)
